subjects.subject: Reading / ELA
topics: Sight words: understands, all, right, work, new, other, any, goes, says, number
Phonics: long i (i_e) and short i
Vocabulary: checks, choose, chores, cost, customers, jobs, spend, tools
studyNotes: Reading comprehension: Ask & answer questions; main idea / details; charts
A chart organizes information into rows or groups. Read its labels and counts before answering a question.
Compare chart values by finding the greatest, least, total, or difference.
Short vowels include a in cat, e in bed, i in sit, o in hot, and u in sun.
Practice identifying sounds in original CVC word examples; they are not a teacher-published test question list.
Ask and answer who, what, where, when, why, and how questions using details from the text.
Compare short i with long i made by the silent-e i_e pattern.
The main idea tells what the whole passage is mostly about; details explain or support it.
A singular possessive noun uses 's to show that one person, animal, place, or thing owns something.

subjects.subject: Spelling / Handwriting
topics: Friday, Oct. 16 test focus: long o / Short
studyNotes: Skill: short and long
Teacher-posted spelling words (page undated): box, side, fox, line, dog, lock, pot, cone, have, home, off, nose, took, poke, rope
Compare short a words like cat with a_e long-a words like game.
Long o sounds like the letter name in go, home, and boat. These are original examples, not an official spelling list.
If a teacher test label also says “short” without naming the vowel, do not guess which short-vowel pattern is included.

subjects.subject: Religion
topics: Unit 1: God Gives Us Life & Love
Chapter 3: Jesus Lives in His Church
Chapter 2: Jesus is God's Best Gift
Chapter 1: God is the Giver of Gifts
studyNotes: Orignial sin; human tendancy to sin which is the result of Adam & Eve's sin
Faith: gift from god tht helps us believe
Sacrament: sacred sign given to the Church by Jesus
At Baptism, oirginal sin is washed away and we recieve the gift of the Holy Spirit and the gift of faith as well as the new life of grace
The Rite (steps) of Baptism
Church members / Christians live as Jesus taught. Church leaders act in Jesus' name and guide the Church.
Jesus is the head of the Church; Mary is the Mother of the Church; we are the body of the Church
Pope Leo; Bishop Schlert
Steps to Baptism: Priest welcomes person; parents / godparents make promises; Bible is read; water is poured; What garment given; candle lit
Jesus is God's greatest gift to us; he tells us about God and teaches us how to live
Jesus gave us the new life of grace
Jesus died for our sins; He is our Savior
Jesus is like a seed. A seed dies for a new plant to grow — Jesus died so we can have new life (grace)
We are called to be disciples, friends of Jesus. Mary is Jesus' mother and the mother of the Church so she is our mother too
The parable of the vine and the branches
Gifts from God
We are made in God's image and likeness; we can think, choose, love
Trinity: 3 persons in one God (Father, Son, Holy Spirit)
We use our senses to enjoy God's gifts
It is our responsibility to take care of God's gifts of creation
We thank God for His gift of creation
Remember: the Trinity is three Persons in one God — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Being made in God's image means people can think, choose, and love.
Caring for creation is one way to show gratitude for God's gifts.
Jesus is our Savior; class notes connect his death and Resurrection with new life in grace.
Original sin is the human tendency to sin connected with Adam and Eve’s sin.
Faith is a gift from God that helps us believe.
A sacrament is a sacred sign given to the Church by Jesus.
At Baptism, original sin is washed away and we receive the Holy Spirit, faith, and new life in grace.
The current Religion lesson calls disciples friends and followers of Jesus.
The current Religion lesson identifies Mary as Jesus’ mother and the mother of the Church.
The current Religion lesson compares a seed dying so a new plant can grow with Jesus dying so we can have new life in grace.
The current Religion lesson connects our senses with noticing and enjoying God’s gifts of creation.
The current Religion lesson names Gifts from God and Chapter 1: God is the Giver of Gifts.
